title: Phishing Awareness
what: Phishing is a deceptive message (email, SMS, chat, QR code) that tries to make you reveal secrets or take a risky action.
why: Most account takeovers and many breaches start with a message that looked routine.
warning_signs: Request for a password or code
Link text that differs from the real destination
safe_practices: Pause and check the sender address
Do not enter credentials from a link; open the site yourself
Verify unusual requests through a known channel
if_it_happens: If you entered a password, change it and tell IT immediately

title: Password Security
what: Passwords prove identity. Strong ones are long, unique and hard to guess.
why: Reused or weak passwords let one leak unlock many accounts.
warning_signs: Passwords stored in notes or spreadsheets
if_it_happens: Change the password and any reused copies

title: Multi-Factor Authentication
what: MFA requires a second proof (app, security key, passkey) in addition to your password.
why: A stolen password alone is not enough to sign in. Strong password + MFA is generally safer than a password alone.
warning_signs: Unexpected MFA prompts you did not start
Requests to read out a code
safe_practices: Prefer authenticator apps or security keys
if_it_happens: Report the prompt flood to IT

title: Social Engineering
what: Manipulating people (not machines) into giving access or information, often by impersonation or pressure.
why: Attackers exploit trust, urgency and authority because it is often easier than hacking.
warning_signs: Claims of authority you cannot verify
safe_practices: Verify identity through a known number
if_it_happens: Tell colleagues who may be targeted

title: Safe Browsing
what: Using the web in ways that reduce exposure to malicious or deceptive sites.
why: Browsers are the main gateway for downloads and logins.
safe_practices: Download software only from official sources
if_it_happens: Run an antivirus scan and tell IT if something was opened

title: Secure Wi-Fi
what: Wi-Fi security means using trusted, encrypted networks and protecting your traffic.
why: Open networks can expose traffic and imitation networks can mislead you.
safe_practices: Use the organization VPN on public Wi-Fi
Turn off auto-join for public networks
if_it_happens: Change passwords used on that network
Report if work accounts were used

title: Software Updates
what: Updates fix security flaws (vulnerabilities) in your software.
why: Attackers commonly target known, unpatched flaws.
safe_practices: Remove software you no longer use
if_it_happens: If a device cannot update, tell IT

title: Ransomware Awareness
what: Ransomware is malware that blocks access to data (often by encryption) and may add data-theft extortion.
why: It can cause downtime, data loss and extortion. Prevention and preparation matter most.
if_it_happens: Disconnect from the network per your policy
Do not pay or negotiate alone
Call IT/security and follow the incident plan

title: USB / Removable Media Safety
what: Removable media can carry malware between systems.
why: Found or shared drives may be deliberately planted.
safe_practices: Do not plug in unknown drives
if_it_happens: Unplug and hand it to IT

title: Data Privacy
what: Protecting personal and sensitive information from misuse or exposure.
why: Leaks harm people and can trigger legal duties.
warning_signs: Sharing files with 'anyone with the link'

title: Mobile Security
what: Protecting phones and tablets and the data on them.
why: Phones hold email, banking and MFA apps.
safe_practices: Install apps only from official stores

title: Remote Work Security
what: Working securely away from the office.
why: Home networks and shared spaces have fewer protections.
warning_signs: Shared family devices used for work
Unknown devices on the home network

title: Cloud Account Security
what: Protecting accounts and data in cloud services.
why: Misconfigured sharing or stolen sessions expose data at scale.

title: Incident Reporting
what: Telling the right people quickly when something looks wrong.
why: Fast reporting limits damage. Reporting a false alarm is always fine.
safe_practices: Do not investigate on your own
if_it_happens: Write down what happened and when
Follow instructions from the response team

title: AI-Enabled Scam Awareness
what: Scams that use AI to imitate voices, faces, or writing style.
why: Convincing fakes make urgency and impersonation more believable.
warning_signs: Unexpected voice or video request for money
Perfect but unusual writing from a 'known' contact
safe_practices: Verify via a second, known channel
if_it_happens: Contact your bank if money moved
